title: TraceRecord
description: One observed run of an agent under adversarial or evaluative conditions: who watched it, what it did, where the artifacts are. Defenders can't learn from what they can't see; a dossier lists every public trace it can find and says plainly when there is none.

kind.description: red_team: the agent was attacked by a researcher · injection_eval: a published test of the agent under adversarial input · ctf: cyber-range or capture-the-flag run · incident: a real-world event with a post-mortem · self_test: this registry's own probe of the agent's public endpoints · vendor_published: a trace bundle the vendor serves at a well-known path

tier.description: 1 reproducible run with public artifacts · 2 third-party report with a transcript or proof of concept · 3 vendor-published evaluation with results only · 4 vendor claim ('we red-teamed it') · 5 nothing found

scope.description: product: this agent · platform: a sibling product on the same platform (Copilot Chat for the Copilot coding agent) · model: the underlying model, not the agent

scenario.description: What was attempted, in one sentence

entry.description: How the adversarial input reached the agent

actions.description: What the agent did (tools called, files read, commands run)

approval.description: Was a human asked before the consequential action?

refused.description: Did the agent refuse or stop?

vendor_response.description: Fix, advisory or CVE, if any

bundle.description: Path of the bundle under data/traces/bundles/, when this registry holds the artifacts

reviewer.description: Who checked the source; null until a person signs it off
